- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum.  
- Underestimate sharp downward turns after spikes; model tends to overreact to recent highs.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecasted mean by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts when recent 18-day history shows strong downward trend; apply a 3–7% downward bias.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often overshoots — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below prior high.  
- Lagged corrections: if true outcome drops 5%+ from 18-day average, adjust next forecast down by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
